1.8.rationale: In the original Indonesian regulation, the scope of regulated “bentuk kekerasan” is defined in Pasal 5–11 (fisik, psikis, seksual, penelantaran, eksploitasi, dan/atau kekerasan lainnya). There is no explicit inclusion of “perdagangan orang” (human trafficking) as a form of violence or as a specific target group/offense in the operative provisions. The only place trafficking appears is in the legal basis list (“Mengingat”, item 7: UU No. 21 Tahun 2007 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang). Merely citing a national law in the legal basis does not mean the local regulation substantively covers trafficking as an indicator in its scope. The retrieved English candidates did contain this context (the legal basis list and the exploitation definition), so a careful judge should still answer No for ‘human trafficking’ unless the indicator is satisfied by mere citation. The judge over-inferred inclusion from a citation, so this is primarily an evaluation/logic error rather than retrieval or translation.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Gorontalo Regency.
2. Regent is the Regent of Gorontalo.
3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
4. Regional Governance is the administration of government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
5. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb.
6. Woman is a person who is female in gender.
7. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological to the victim.
8. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, and other violence.
10. Victim is women and children who experience misery and/or suffering either directly or ...
11. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will, is, or has occurred.
12. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
14. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
15. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Region to provide services in the context of empowerment of women and children victims of acts of violence.
16. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the accompaniment process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and danger from perpetrators.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and ... in the household.
19. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence, hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK, is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

CHAPTER VIII

Article 40
At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of Women and Children in the Region are declared to remain valid insofar as they have not been replaced and do not conflict with the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:

c. conducting independent socialization of women's and children's rights,
d. providing first aid to victims,
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

b. safely and comfortably,
c. a sense of empathy,
d. non-discrimination; easily accessible; free of charge; and guaranteed confidentiality.

Article 16

a. preventing the occurrence of violence against women and children,
b. reporting if violence occurs, protecting victims; and
d. providing emergency assistance.

6.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text does not specifically address “women victims of trafficking” as an intersectional group. It regulates protection for “perempuan dan anak korban kekerasan” generally (e.g., Pasal 3, Pasal 14, Pasal 23–31) and defines “eksploitasi” broadly (Pasal 10) but does not mention “korban perdagangan orang” or tailor provisions to trafficking survivors. As with discrepancy 1.8, trafficking is only referenced in the legal basis (UU No. 21 Tahun 2007) and not operationalized as a specific victim category. The retrieved passages shown to the judge included the legal basis citation and general victim-protection provisions; the judge again treated the citation as proof of substantive coverage of trafficking victims. That inference is flawed given the Indonesian ground truth, so the discrepancy is best explained by evaluation failure (overly lenient reasoning), not by missing evidence or mistranslation.
